newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-ACB IN ROW WITH PLAYERS OVER NEGOTIATOR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ACB IN ROW WITH PLAYERS OVER NEGOTIATOR.

text.p: The Australian Cricket Board (ACB) was set on a collision course with leading players on Tuesday after refusing to accept former board official Graham Halbish as the players' representative in future pay talks.
ACB officials have said they will not deal with Halbish, who worked as ACB chief executive for four years before he was sacked three months ago, because of his inside knowledge.
But the fledgling Australian Cricketers' Association on Tuesday stood firm, insisting that Halbish would act on their behalf after employing him as a negotiator.
Halbish left the ACB in acrimonious circumstances in January. The two parties reached an out-of-court settlement last month after Halbish began legal action for unfair dismissal.
"We've had legal advice that Graham can act for us...The whole of the membership base is fully behind his appointment," association president Tim May said.
"I don't see it as a hindrance (Halbish's previous association with the ACB), it doesn't affect us," said May, who described the appointment as a coup for players.
The players' union has about 80 members and is open to past and present first-class cricketers, the ACB said.
ACB chairman Denis Rogers has announced he will refuse to negotiate with Halbish because of his knowledge of information relating to player contracts and board finances.

Speaking to reporters during Australia's just-concluded tour to South Africa, Rogers said: "A lot of the information belongs to the Australian Cricket Board and he (Halbish), as a former employee, has a duty to restrict use of that information."
Rogers and May are scheduled to meet for talks on Friday, an ACB spokesman said.
